sample_memories.text: Rhea's primary dataset is CoheReD-v2, 4,120 annotated academic abstracts with span-level coherence labels.
Her proposed method is called SpanRank; the ablated variant without relation features is SpanRank-flat.
Her advisor is Prof. Helena Broughton; her second supervisor is Dr. Tomas Reinhardt.
Frequent coauthors: Yuki Tanabe (Kyoto), Priya Raghavan (IIT Madras).
Recurring claim: entity-grid baselines degrade sharply past 500 tokens, which motivates the span-level formulation.
Baselines she always compares against: Barzilay and Lapata entity grid, LongCoh, and a fine-tuned Longformer.
She reports Krippendorff's alpha rather than Cohen's kappa because her annotation has three annotators.
Cluster access is on the 'artemis' GPU partition, jobs submitted through Slurm with the account code inf-nlp-24.
Reviewer 2 on her last submission argued the entity-grid baseline was undertuned; she now reports a tuned and untuned variant of every baseline.
CoheReD-v2 was annotated by three annotators with Krippendorff's alpha of 0.71 on the span-level labels.
She is a teaching assistant for INFR11125 Text Technologies, tutorial group 4, Thursdays.
Cluster jobs: sbatch on the artemis partition, account inf-nlp-24, always with --time=08:00:00 because the default walltime kills long runs.
Yuki Tanabe handles the figures and plotting on their joint papers; Rhea writes the analysis sections.
She walks with a Sunday group in the Pentlands, usually meeting at Flotterstone.

study_design.graph_signature: Roughly eighteen months of accumulated use. Deep and narrow: method names, dataset names, coauthors, recurring claims, and the relations between them are well populated in Neo4j.
study_design.why_in_study: Provides the upper bound case for relation based retrieval. If graph grounding never helps here, it is unlikely to help anywhere.
study_design.expected_behavioral_signature: Largest acceptance gain under KG-ON, concentrated on noun phrases and citations. Low post acceptance edit distance. Time to decision runs long because verifying a retrieved citation costs more than skimming a generic phrase.
study_design.instrumentation_note: Best case for memory type attribution: retrieved items are almost all semantic, so a mixed attribution profile would flag a retrieval bug rather than a user difference.
study_design.ethical_handling: Buffer contains unpublished results. Logging is scoped to declared drafting sessions and the trace is reviewed before analysis.

sample_memories.text: Client Orbital Freight: staging cluster is orb-stg-euw1, production is orb-prd-euw1. Deploys go through 'make deploy ENV=stg' never kubectl apply directly.

Client Calder Health: HIPAA-adjacent. No production access from personal laptop; always jump through the bastion at bastion.calder.internal with the yubikey.
Client Vantage Media: legacy, still on Docker Compose. Restart order is postgres, then redis, then api, then worker.
Iman's standard rollback sequence: helm rollback <release> <previous-revision> --wait, then verify with kubectl rollout status, then post in the client channel.
He always runs terraform plan -out=tfplan and applies the saved plan file, never a bare terraform apply.
Naming convention across his clients: <client-prefix>-<env>-<region-short>, region-short uses euw1, use1, aps1.
Calder Health postmortems use a blameless template kept in the calder-runbooks repo under templates/postmortem.md.
Invoices go out on the first of the month, NET 15, raised in Wave with the client PO number in the reference field.
Orbital Freight incident channel is #orb-incidents; he posts a status line there before and after every rollback.
His reusable Terraform module set lives in the haddad-systems/tf-modules repo, versioned with git tags like v0.4.2.

study_design.graph_signature: Command sequences, config conventions, repository and host naming, per client ordering of routine operations.
study_design.why_in_study: Correctness is visible at a glance, so accept and dismiss approach a clean relevance judgment with almost no deliberation cost.

sample_memories.text: Sofia opens essays with a small concrete scene before naming the argument, usually within the first three sentences.
She prefers 'attention' to 'focus', avoids the word 'journey', and never uses 'unpack' as a verb.
Recurring position: convenience is not the opposite of effort, it is the relocation of effort onto someone else.
Themes she returns to: walkability, the cost of frictionlessness, the ethics of attention, Nordic post-war housing.
She uses em-dashes sparingly and favours short declarative sentences after a long one, as a rhythm device.
Previous pieces: 'The Fifteen Minute Alibi' (walkability), 'Nothing To Do In Vallingby' (post-war housing), 'The Ninety Second Rule' (attention).
Her newsletter sign-off is always a single line, no exhortation to subscribe or share.
Her commissioning editor at The Coastal Review is Ines Duarte; pitches go to her directly, two paragraphs maximum.
Her reusable festival bio: 'Sofia Lindqvist writes about cities, attention and the things we stop noticing.'
She answers reader email in the same register as the newsletter, never with a template, and always signs off with just her first name.
Her newsletter is called The Long Way Round and publishes Thursdays at 07:00.

target_memories: Opens with a concrete scene then names the argument

sample_memories.text: Arjun works at Kestrel Retail Group as an operations associate.
He asked about formatting a resignation letter two weeks ago.
He is based in Bengaluru.
He asked for a chicken curry recipe on his first day using the tool.
He is dealing with a rental deposit that has not been returned.
He asked how to word a leave request to his manager last week.
His manager at Kestrel Retail Group is called Divya.

tasks.title: Email the former landlord about a deposit
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Write a firm but polite email chasing a rental deposit that is six weeks overdue.
tasks.typed_prefix:
Dear Mr Prasad,

I am writing to follow up on the security deposit for
tasks.expected_completion: the flat I vacated in July. It has now been six weeks and I have not received the refund or an itemised deduction list.
tasks.tests: The one task where his sparse graph has a genuinely relevant memory. KG-ON should help slightly here and nowhere else.

tasks.title: Fill in a course application form
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Complete the free-text fields on an application for a part-time data analytics course.
tasks.typed_prefix: Why do you want to take this course? I currently work in
tasks.expected_completion: retail operations and want to move into a reporting role, so I need SQL and dashboarding beyond spreadsheets.
target_memories: Goal: move into an analyst role
tasks.tests: Sparse retrieval failure mode. Watch whether the resignation-letter memory is pulled in here and produces an irrelevant completion.

tasks.title: Message a friend about weekend plans
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Reply to a friend proposing a trip this weekend.
tasks.typed_prefix: yeah I'm free saturday, was thinking we could drive out to
tasks.expected_completion: Coorg if we leave early, otherwise Nandi Hills is easier.
tasks.tests: Lower bound. KG-ON should be indistinguishable from KG-OFF; a large delta here indicates the effect comes from prompt length rather than graph content.

tasks.title: Report an inventory discrepancy
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Email your manager about a stock count that does not match the system.
tasks.typed_prefix:
Hi Divya,

The Tuesday count for the Whitefield store is off by
tasks.expected_completion: eleven units on the same SKU as last month, so I think it is a receiving error rather than shrinkage.
tasks.tests: One of the few tasks where his thin graph holds a directly relevant fact.

tasks.title: Comment on a practice SQL query
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Annotate a query you wrote for the analytics course.
tasks.typed_prefix: -- joining on store_id because
tasks.expected_completion: -- WEAK: no stored memory covers his schema or coursework
tasks.tests: True null case. Any confident completion here is a hallucination rather than a retrieval.

tasks.title: Follow up on a resignation letter
tasks.context_given_to_participant: You drafted a resignation letter earlier and decided against sending it. Write to a friend about it.
tasks.typed_prefix: I never sent that letter in the end. Decided to wait until
tasks.expected_completion: the analytics certificate is finished, then move properly instead of just leaving.
tasks.tests: The resignation memory is genuinely relevant here. Contrast with P5-T10, where it is not.

tasks.title: Ask a cooking question
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Ask a friend how to fix a dish that went wrong.
tasks.typed_prefix: the curry came out way too sour, is it
tasks.expected_completion: the tomatoes or did I add the tamarind too early?
target_memories: Asked for a chicken curry recipe on day one
tasks.tests: Tests whether a single old episodic memory is retrieved appropriately when the domain actually matches.

tasks.title: Fill in a gym signup form
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Complete the free-text goal field on a membership form.
tasks.typed_prefix: What are you hoping to achieve? Mainly consistency, aiming for
tasks.expected_completion: three sessions a week rather than anything specific.
target_memories: Goal: gym three times a week
tasks.tests: Single-memory match on a form field. Small positive delta expected, and little else.

tasks.title: Request leave from your manager
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Ask for two days off next month.
tasks.typed_prefix:
Hi Divya,

I would like to take the 14th and 15th off to
tasks.expected_completion: travel, I have no open reconciliations that week and can hand over the vendor calls.
target_memories: Asked how to word a leave request last week
tasks.tests: Two thin memories combine. Watch whether both are retrieved or only the more recent one.

tasks.title: Enquire about guitar lessons
tasks.context_given_to_participant: Ask a local teacher about beginner lessons.
tasks.typed_prefix: Hi, I am a complete beginner and wanted to ask about
tasks.expected_completion: -- TRAP: unrelated domain; deposit and resignation memories likely over-retrieved here
target_memories: None relevant; expect deposit or resignation memory to intrude
tasks.tests: The sparse over-retrieval failure mode, isolated. With so few memories stored, irrelevant ones get pulled into unrelated prompts.

study_design.graph_signature: Under forty stored memories and very few relations, so the Neo4j layer contributes little beyond what the vector index already returns.
study_design.why_in_study: Addresses the confound named in the limitations, that graphs differ in size as well as in kind. He supplies the near zero delta against which the other four are read.
study_design.expected_behavioral_signature: KG-ON should sit close to KG-OFF on all four measures. A large delta here would suggest the effect comes from prompt length or scaffold differences rather than from graph content.
study_design.instrumentation_note: Also surfaces the sparse retrieval failure mode, where the same one or two memories are pulled into unrelated prompts.
study_design.ethical_handling: Lowest sensitivity of the five, which makes him the appropriate participant for any example trace shown in the paper.
study_design.measure_stressed: All four, as a lower bound
study_design.sparse_failure_mode_note: With so few memories, expect the resignation-letter and deposit memories to be pulled into unrelated prompts. That over-retrieval is itself a logged finding.
